subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trust lifecycle for generated HTML after outbound staging once this PR is rebased?
rationale: The patch is a plausible best fix for the reported message-loss bug, but it deliberately changes which staged HTML files can pass a trusted host-read gate, so automation should not treat that boundary decision as routine code review.

options.title: Rebase and accept provenance lifecycle
options.body: Resolve current-main conflicts, keep the sha256/size read-once checks and stale-row cleanup, then merge after maintainer/security signoff.

options.title: Require tighter lifecycle before merge
options.body: Ask for additional bounds such as TTL-based row cleanup, chunked pruning, or a different marker lifecycle if the current provenance table behavior is not acceptable.

options.title: Reject the boundary expansion
options.body: Close or replace the PR if maintainers decide outbound-staged HTML should not be trusted even with content-bound provenance.

recommendation.title: Rebase and accept provenance lifecycle
recommendation.body: Resolve current-main conflicts, keep the sha256/size read-once checks and stale-row cleanup, then merge after maintainer/security signoff.

likelyOwner.reason: The original trusted generated HTML host-read seam and shared outbound attachment history make this the strongest security-boundary routing signal.
